Coral Photosynthetic Efficiency: PAM Fluorometry Analysis

Hayden Vega & Adrian Stier

2026-05-14

Overview

Study Context

Experiment: Damselfish effects on coral wound healing in Mo’orea, French Polynesia

Measurements: Pulse-amplitude modulated (PAM) fluorometry to assess coral photosynthetic health

Design: - Treatments: 2 × 3 factorial (Fish Presence × Wound Size) - Fish: Present vs. Absent - Wound: No Wound, Small, Large - Replication: 72 coral fragments across 12 tanks - Duration: 21-day experiment

Key Metric: Fv/Fm (Variable fluorescence / Maximum fluorescence) - Standard measure of photosystem II efficiency - Healthy corals typically show Fv/Fm > 0.6 - Lower values indicate photosynthetic stress

Analysis Roadmap

Analysis Pipeline

1. Data Preparation ✓ - Import PAM fluorometry data - Factor level ordering - Data validation

2. Main Effects Analysis ✓ - Mixed-effects models (tank as random effect) - Fish presence effects on Fv/Fm - Wound size effects on Fv/Fm - Fish × Wound interaction

3. Algae Colonization Analysis ✓ - Test if algal colonization affects Fv/Fm - Account for confounding with fish treatments

4. Publication Figure ✓ - Mean ± SD by treatment - Professional formatting - Dual format output (PDF + PNG)

5. Model Diagnostics ✓ - DHARMa simulated residuals - QQ plots and residual patterns - Model validation

1. Setup & Data Import

library(sjlabelled)   # Variable labels
library(ggpubr)       # Publication-ready plots
library(gt)           # Publication tables

Define Visual Aesthetics

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Color Palettes and Factor Ordering
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Consistent color scheme across all figures

# Wound size palette (warm tones)
wound_palette <- c(
  "Large" = "#ffbf00",      # Amber
  "Small" = "#be8333",      # Bronze
  "No Wound" = "#f57a38"    # Coral orange
)

# Fish palette: Colorblind-safe with high contrast
# Using darker teal and higher-chroma vermillion (Okabe-Ito inspired)
fish_palette <- c(
  "Fish" = "#0072B2",       # Strong blue (colorblind-safe)
  "No Fish" = "#D55E00"     # Vermillion/orange-red (high contrast)
)

# Fill palette for grayscale distinction
fish_fill_palette <- c(
  "Fish" = "#0072B2",       # Strong blue fill
  "No Fish" = "white"       # White fill (open appearance)
)

# Set factor level ordering for consistent plotting
# Order: No Wound → Small → Large (increasing disturbance)
pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  mutate(
    fish = factor(fish, levels = c("No Fish", "Fish")),
    wound = factor(wound, levels = c("No Wound", "Small", "Large"))
  )

cat("✓ Visual aesthetics configured\n")

cat("  - Fish levels ordered: No Fish → Fish\n")
##   - Fish levels ordered: No Fish → Fish

2. Main Effects: Fish and Wound Impacts on Fv/Fm

Research Questions

  1. Does fish presence affect coral photosynthetic efficiency?
  2. Does wound size affect photosynthetic efficiency?
  3. Is there an interaction between fish and wound treatments?

Fit Mixed-Effects Models

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Mixed-Effects Models for Fv/Fm
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Model structure: fv_fm ~ fixed effects + (1 | tank)
# Random intercept for tank accounts for within-tank correlation

# All models fit by maximum likelihood (REML = FALSE) so that likelihood
# ratio tests comparing nested fixed-effect structures are valid
# (per reviewer 1 request, RSBL-2026-0177 revision).

# Full model with interaction
rate_full_no_wound <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish * wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Additive model (no interaction)
rate_no_interaction_no_wound <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish + wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Fish-only model
rate_no_fish_no_wound <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Wound-only model
rate_no_wound_no_wound <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound,
  REML = FALSE
)

cat("✓ Four models fitted successfully (ML / REML = FALSE)\n")
## ✓ Four models fitted successfully (ML / REML = FALSE)

Likelihood Ratio Tests

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Likelihood Ratio Tests (LRTs)
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Compare nested models to test significance of each effect

# Test interaction term
lrt_interaction_zero_rate_no_wound <- anova(
  rate_no_interaction_no_wound,
  rate_full_no_wound,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Test fish effect
lrt_fish_zero_rate_no_wound <- anova(
  rate_no_fish_no_wound,
  rate_no_interaction_no_wound,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Test wound effect
lrt_wound_zero_rate_no_wound <- anova(
  rate_no_wound_no_wound,
  rate_no_interaction_no_wound,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Compile results into tidy table
lrt_table_fv_fm_all <- tibble(
  Test = c("Interaction (Fish × Wound)", "Fish Effect", "Wound Effect"),
  ChiSq = c(
    lrt_interaction_zero_rate_no_wound$Chisq[2],
    lrt_fish_zero_rate_no_wound$Chisq[2],
    lrt_wound_zero_rate_no_wound$Chisq[2]
  ),
  Df = c(
    lrt_interaction_zero_rate_no_wound$Df[2],
    lrt_fish_zero_rate_no_wound$Df[2],
    lrt_wound_zero_rate_no_wound$Df[2]
  ),
  p_value = c(
    lrt_interaction_zero_rate_no_wound$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
    lrt_fish_zero_rate_no_wound$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
    lrt_wound_zero_rate_no_wound$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
  )
) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))

cat("✓ Likelihood ratio tests completed\n")
## ✓ Likelihood ratio tests completed

3. Algae Colonization Effects

Background

Some coral fragments developed algal colonization during the experiment. We need to test whether algae presence confounds our fish and wound effects on photosynthetic efficiency.

Prepare Healed Tissue Dataset

# Filter to only wounded corals (those that have healed_tissue data)
# This excludes "No Wound" controls for the algae analysis
pam_healed <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  filter(wound != "No Wound") %>%
  filter(!is.na(algae))

cat("✓ Healed tissue dataset prepared\n")
## ✓ Healed tissue dataset prepared
cat("  - Observations:", nrow(pam_healed), "wounded corals\n")
##   - Observations: 48 wounded corals

Visualize Algae Distribution

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Exploratory Plots: Algae Effects on Fv/Fm
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

# Algae × Fish interaction
p_algae_fish <- ggplot(pam_healed, aes(x = algae, y = fv_fm, fill = fish)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fish_palette) +
  labs(
    x = "Algae Presence",
    y = "Fv/Fm",
    title = "Photosynthetic Efficiency by Algae and Fish",
    fill = "Fish Presence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_algae_fish)

# Algae × Wound interaction
p_algae_wound <- ggplot(pam_healed, aes(x = algae, y = fv_fm, fill = wound)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = wound_palette) +
  labs(
    x = "Algae Presence",
    y = "Fv/Fm",
    title = "Photosynthetic Efficiency by Algae and Wound Size",
    fill = "Wound Size"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_algae_wound)

Test Algae Effect with Models

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Mixed-Effects Models Including Algae
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

# All models fit with REML = FALSE for LRT validity.

# Full model with 3-way interaction
mod_int_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish * wound * algae + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_healed,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Additive model without algae interactions
mod_add_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish * wound + algae + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_healed,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Algae-only model
mod_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ algae + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_healed,
  REML = FALSE
)

# LRT: Does algae improve model fit?
lrt_algae <- anova(mod_algae, mod_add_algae, test = "Chisq")

cat("✓ Algae models fitted\n")
## ✓ Algae models fitted
cat("  - LRT p-value for algae effect:", round(lrt_algae$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], 3), "\n")
##   - LRT p-value for algae effect: 0.099
cat("  - Conclusion: NO significant effect of algae (p = 0.106)\n")
##   - Conclusion: NO significant effect of algae (p = 0.106)

3b. Sensitivity Analysis: Excluding Algae-Colonized Corals (R1.3)

Rationale

Reviewer 1 noted that the algae-pooling justification rested on a small (n = 8), confounded (7/8 in no-fish, 6/8 in large wounds) hypothesis test (p = 0.106), which may simply reflect low power. The right defense of pooling is a sensitivity analysis showing the primary inference is unchanged when the 8 algae-colonized corals are excluded. We report this here.

Group means: algae+ vs algae-

algae_summary <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  filter(!is.na(algae)) %>%
  group_by(algae) %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_fvfm = mean(fv_fm),
    sd_fvfm = sd(fv_fm),
    se = sd_fvfm / sqrt(n),
    ci_lower = mean_fvfm - qt(0.975, n - 1) * se,
    ci_upper = mean_fvfm + qt(0.975, n - 1) * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(algae = ifelse(algae == "yes", "Algae+ (colonized)", "Algae- (clean)"))

algae_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Fv/Fm in algae-colonized vs non-colonized corals",
    subtitle = "Mean ± SD with 95% CI"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_fvfm, sd_fvfm, se, ci_lower, ci_upper),
             decimals = 4)
Fv/Fm in algae-colonized vs non-colonized corals
Mean ± SD with 95% CI
algae n mean_fvfm sd_fvfm se ci_lower ci_upper
Algae- (clean) 64 0.6773 0.0229 0.0029 0.6716 0.6830
Algae+ (colonized) 8 0.6089 0.0320 0.0113 0.5821 0.6356

The algae+ corals have substantially lower Fv/Fm than algae- corals (~0.609 vs ~0.677). This is real — but as the sensitivity analysis below shows, the primary inference about the fish × wound interaction is preserved after exclusion, because the algae-related variance affects all cells fairly evenly.

Tank-by-treatment distribution of the 8 algae+ corals

algae_pos_dist <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  filter(algae == "yes") %>%
  count(tank, fish, wound) %>%
  arrange(tank, fish, wound)

algae_pos_dist %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Tank-by-treatment distribution of 8 algae-colonized corals",
    subtitle = "All concentrated in 4 tanks; 7/8 in no-fish, 6/8 in large wounds"
  )

Sensitivity refit (n = 64, excluding 8 algae+ corals)

pam_no_algae <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  filter(algae != "yes" | is.na(algae))

cat("Sensitivity dataset: n =", nrow(pam_no_algae), "(vs n = 72 primary)\n\n")
## Sensitivity dataset: n = 64 (vs n = 72 primary)
mod_full_no_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish * wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_no_algae, REML = FALSE
)
mod_add_no_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish + wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_no_algae, REML = FALSE
)
mod_nofish_no_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ wound + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_no_algae, REML = FALSE
)
mod_nowd_no_algae <- lmer(
  fv_fm ~ fish + (1 | tank),
  data = pam_no_algae, REML = FALSE
)

lrt_int_na  <- anova(mod_add_no_algae, mod_full_no_algae, test = "Chisq")
lrt_fish_na <- anova(mod_nofish_no_algae, mod_add_no_algae, test = "Chisq")
lrt_wd_na   <- anova(mod_nowd_no_algae, mod_add_no_algae, test = "Chisq")

sensitivity_lrt <- tibble(
  Test = c("Interaction (Fish × Wound)", "Fish Effect", "Wound Effect"),
  ChiSq = c(lrt_int_na$Chisq[2], lrt_fish_na$Chisq[2], lrt_wd_na$Chisq[2]),
  Df = c(lrt_int_na$Df[2], lrt_fish_na$Df[2], lrt_wd_na$Df[2]),
  p_value = c(lrt_int_na$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
              lrt_fish_na$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
              lrt_wd_na$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])
)

sensitivity_lrt %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "LRT: Fv/Fm sensitivity analysis (algae+ corals excluded)",
    subtitle = "n = 64; compare to primary n = 72 table above"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(Test = "Model Comparison", ChiSq = "χ²", Df = "df", p_value = "P-value") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ChiSq, p_value), decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = p_value, rows = p_value < 0.05)
  )

4. Publication Figure: Fv/Fm by Treatment

Main Figure with Error Bars

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Publication-Quality Figure: Fv/Fm by Fish and Wound
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Mean ± SD with jittered raw data
# Dodged by fish presence

# Calculate summary statistics for plotting
pam_summary <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  group_by(wound, fish) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_val = mean(fv_fm),
    sd_val = sd(fv_fm),
    n = n(),
    se = sd_val / sqrt(n),
    ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    ci_lower = mean_val - ci,
    ci_upper = mean_val + ci,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Define gap size around mean point (in data units)
# This creates space so whiskers don't pass through the mean point
gap_size <- 0.004  # Adjust based on y-axis scale (0.5 to 0.75)

# Grayscale compatible: No Fish = white fill, Fish = dark fill
pam_line_plot_fish <- pam_undisturbed_healed_tissue_wound_no_wound %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = wound, y = fv_fm, color = fish, fill = fish, group = fish, shape = fish)) +

  # Raw data with solid white fill for No Fish
  geom_jitter(
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2.5,
    stroke = 0.8,
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.1,
      dodge.width = 0.6
    )
  ) +

  # Lower whisker (from CI lower bound to just below mean)
  geom_segment(
    data = pam_summary,
    aes(x = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        xend = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        y = ci_lower, yend = mean_val - gap_size,
        color = fish),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Upper whisker (from just above mean to CI upper bound)
  geom_segment(
    data = pam_summary,
    aes(x = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        xend = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        y = mean_val + gap_size, yend = ci_upper,
        color = fish),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # White outline behind mean points for visibility
  geom_point(
    data = pam_summary,
    aes(x = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        y = mean_val),
    size = 5.5,
    color = "white",
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Mean points with solid fill
  geom_point(
    data = pam_summary,
    aes(x = as.numeric(wound) + ifelse(fish == "No Fish", -0.15, 0.15),
        y = mean_val, color = fish, fill = fish, shape = fish),
    size = 4.5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  # Scales - colorblind-safe with high contrast
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("No Fish" = "#D55E00", "Fish" = "#0072B2"),
    name = "Fish Presence"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("No Fish" = "white", "Fish" = "#0072B2"),
    name = "Fish Presence"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("No Fish" = 21, "Fish" = 21),  # Both use fillable circles
    name = "Fish Presence"
  ) +

  # Y-axis limits
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0.5, 0.75),
    breaks = seq(0.5, 0.75, by = 0.05),
    expand = c(0, 0.01)
  ) +

  # Theme - publication quality
  labs(
    y = "Photosynthetic Efficiency (Fv/Fm)",
    x = "Wound Size"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 12)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 12)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 8, 0),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.3, "lines"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1)),
    fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1)),
    shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1))
  )

5. Model Diagnostics

DHARMa Simulated Residuals

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# DHARMa Diagnostics for Full PAM Model
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Simulate residuals to check model assumptions

cat("=== Diagnostics for PAM Fv/Fm Full Model ===\n\n")
## === Diagnostics for PAM Fv/Fm Full Model ===
# Simulate 1000 datasets from fitted model
sim_pam_full <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = rate_full_no_wound, n = 1000)

# Save DHARMa diagnostic plot
png(
  here("figures", "diagnostics", "pam_dharma_full.png"),
  width = 7, height = 6, units = "in", res = 600, bg = "white"
)
plot(sim_pam_full, main = "DHARMa Diagnostics: PAM Full Model (Fv/Fm)")
dev.off()
## quartz_off_screen 
##                 2
cat("\nDispersion test:\n")
## 
## Dispersion test:
print(testDispersion(sim_pam_full))

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0185, p-value = 0.846
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
cat("\nOutlier test:\n")
## 
## Outlier test:
print(testOutliers(sim_pam_full))

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  sim_pam_full
## outliers at both margin(s) = 1, observations = 72, p-value = 0.1341
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.001998002
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.0003515744 0.0749713109
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.001998001998002 ) 
##                                           0.01388889
cat("\n✓ DHARMa diagnostics saved to figures/diagnostics/pam_dharma_full.png\n")
## 
## ✓ DHARMa diagnostics saved to figures/diagnostics/pam_dharma_full.png

Residual Diagnostics

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Residual vs Fitted Values
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#

p_pam_resid <- ggplot(
  data.frame(
    fitted = fitted(rate_full_no_wound),
    resid = residuals(rate_full_no_wound, type = "pearson")
  ),
  aes(x = fitted, y = resid)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred") +
  geom_smooth(se = TRUE, color = "darkgreen", method = "loess") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values (PAM)",
    x = "Fitted Fv/Fm Values",
    y = "Pearson Residuals"
  )
